meta.title: Napoleon Had Everything. It Wasn't Enough.
meta.working_title: Napoleon Had Everything. It Wasn't Enough.
meta.device: Napoleon's black bicorne hat. It sits on a schoolboy's desk at Brienne, then on his head at Toulon, on a cushion at Notre-Dame, in the snow on the road from Moscow, on the mud at Waterloo, and in the last shot on a hook at Longwood on Saint Helena, with the sea in the window behind it. A map of Europe returns in every act, and French blue spreads over it, then drains away.
meta.style: 2D dynamic, locked Village Painterly look: 6-head characters from the village-cast rig in period dress (Corsican village clothes, cadet uniforms, revolutionary tricolour sashes, French line infantry in blue, Austrian white, Russian green, British redcoats, Imperial Guard bearskins, Empire-style gowns). Napoleon keeps one face sheet through five ages (9, 24, 35, 43, 51). Highly detailed painted backgrounds with warm light and dynamic cast shadows: a Corsican hill town, a school dormitory, Toulon harbour at night, Alpine passes, the Pyramids, Notre-Dame with candles, the frozen Pratzen Heights, burning Moscow, the snow road, Fontainebleau, Waterloo's muddy ridge, foggy Longwood. Moving cameras, 3 to 5 parallax layers, characters act in every shot, match cuts. Battles are shown through movement, smoke and maps; no gore. SFX under the VO; music added at combine.
meta.source: 'The Man Who Conquered Europe But Never Conquered Himself' (Pushpam upload, batch 4). The source was slow English for language learners (~3,700 words). Rewritten at our pace (~1,400 words), fact-checked; several errors fixed (see list).

shots.vo: June 1812. Napoleon Bonaparte leads the biggest army Europe has ever seen, more than six hundred thousand men, across a river into Russia.
shots.visual: A huge army crossing pontoon bridges over a wide river at dawn; columns of blue uniforms, horses and cannons stretch to the horizon.
shots.anim: Slow crane up from the bridge to the endless columns.

shots.vo: Six months later, only a small fraction of them come back, through the snow, starving and frozen.
shots.visual: The same road in winter: a thin line of ragged soldiers in blankets, a broken cart, a black hat lying in the snow.
shots.anim: Snow falls; the camera drifts down to the hat.

shots.vo: He was the most powerful man in Europe. He had crowns, palaces and an empire. And every time he won, he wanted more.
shots.visual: Quick images: a crown on a cushion, a palace hall, the map of Europe turning blue.
shots.anim: Each image slides in like a card.

shots.visual: Title over the black bicorne hat in the snow, wind lifting the flakes.
shots.anim: Snow swirls; the title fades up.

shots.vo: He was born in 1769 on Corsica, an island France had taken over just the year before. Napoleone di Buonaparte grew up speaking Italian.
shots.visual: A Corsican hill town of stone houses over the sea; a small boy runs down a stepped lane.
shots.anim: Sea glitters; laundry flaps; the boy runs past the camera.

shots.vo: At nine, he was sent to a military school in France. He had a thick accent and little money, and the other boys mocked him.
shots.visual: A school dormitory: rich boys laughing and pointing; the small Corsican boy sits alone on his bed with a book.
shots.anim: The laughing boys sway; the boy turns a page without looking up.

shots.vo: So he read. Maths, history, battles. He became an artillery officer at sixteen.
shots.visual: Candlelight: the boy at a desk piled with books, a black bicorne hat beside him; then the young officer in a blue coat by a cannon.
shots.anim: Match cut from the boy's candle to the cannon's fuse.

shots.vo: Then in 1789 the French Revolution broke the old order. Nobles fled or lost their heads. Suddenly, talent could matter more than birth.
shots.visual: Paris: crowds with tricolour flags, a toppled royal statue; an aristocrat's carriage racing away.
shots.anim: Flags wave; the carriage rattles off screen.

shots.vo: In 1793, British and Spanish ships held the port of Toulon. Captain Bonaparte, aged twenty-four, saw where to put the cannons. His guns drove the ships from the harbour, and he was made a general.
shots.visual: Night at Toulon harbour: Napoleon points from a hill; cannons fire; ships in the bay pull away under smoke.
shots.anim: Muzzle flashes light the smoke; the ships turn away.

shots.vo: In 1796 he took over a hungry, ragged army in Italy. In about a year, he beat Austrian army after Austrian army.
shots.visual: Ragged French soldiers on an Alpine road; Napoleon on horseback pointing down to the green plains of Italy.
shots.anim: The army pours down the pass; the map turns blue around northern Italy.

shots.vo: In 1798 he sailed to Egypt with an army and over a hundred and fifty scientists. But the British navy destroyed his fleet, and his army was trapped.
shots.visual: Napoleon before the Pyramids with soldiers and scholars measuring; then ships burning in a bay at night.
shots.anim: Scholars sketch; then a fireball lights the bay.

shots.vo: So he left his army behind, slipped back to France, and told everyone it was a triumph.
shots.visual: A small ship sailing at night; Napoleon on deck looking back at the dark coast; then Paris crowds cheering.
shots.anim: The ship slips into the dark; wipe to cheering crowds.

shots.vo: In November 1799, he seized power with soldiers. He was thirty and ran France.
shots.visual: A government hall: soldiers with bayonets push in; politicians climb out of windows.
shots.anim: Doors burst open; a politician scrambles out of a window.

shots.vo: On the second of December 1804, in Notre-Dame, the Pope came to crown him. Napoleon took the crown and put it on his own head.
shots.visual: Notre-Dame full of candles; the Pope seated; Napoleon lifts a golden laurel crown over his own head.
shots.anim: Candles flicker; the crown rises slowly; the Pope's eyebrows rise.

acts.name: Act 3: The Top of the World

shots.vo: One year later, at Austerlitz, the armies of Austria and Russia faced him. They had more men and held the high ground.
shots.visual: Frozen fields at dawn; Russian and Austrian columns on a hill; Napoleon on a smaller hill watching through a telescope.
shots.anim: Fog rolls across the valley; the telescope glints.

shots.vo: Napoleon made his right side look weak. The enemy came down off the heights to attack it. Then he sent his army straight up the middle onto the empty heights, and cut them in two.
shots.visual: The battle map: red arrows go down to the French right; then a big blue arrow drives up the middle and splits them.
shots.anim: Arrows draw themselves; the enemy block splits in two.

shots.vo: It became his most famous victory. Within a year, the thousand-year-old Holy Roman Empire was gone, and his brothers were kings of Naples, Holland and Westphalia.
shots.visual: The map of Europe filling with blue; three brothers in crowns appear over their kingdoms.
shots.anim: Blue floods across the map; crowns pop onto heads.

shots.vo: But he could not beat Britain at sea. So in 1806 he banned all of Europe from trading with Britain. Smuggling boomed, his allies suffered, and Britain kept trading with the world.
shots.visual: A French port with a CLOSED sign on a warehouse; at night smugglers rowing crates ashore; a British ship sailing past.
shots.anim: The sign swings; lanterns bob on the smugglers' boat.

shots.vo: In 1808 he made his brother Joseph king of Spain. The Spanish rose up in a new kind of war: the guerrilla, the little war. Ambushes in the hills, year after year.
shots.visual: A Spanish mountain road: villagers with muskets hidden on rocks above a French supply column; smoke from an ambush.
shots.anim: Muskets pop from the rocks; horses rear.

shots.vo: He called it his Spanish ulcer. Six years of war that drained him of men.
shots.visual: Napoleon at a map table jabbing at Spain; an aide hands him another casualty list.
shots.anim: He crumples the list; candles flicker.

shots.vo: He had no son with his wife Josephine, so in 1809 he divorced her, and married an Austrian princess, Marie Louise. She gave him an heir.
shots.visual: Josephine in tears signing a paper; then a royal wedding; then a baby in a golden cradle.
shots.anim: Wipe from Josephine's tear to the wedding candles.

shots.vo: Then the Tsar of Russia began trading with Britain again. Napoleon's answer was the Grande Armée: men from France, Poland, Italy, Germany and more.
shots.visual: Tsar Alexander tearing up a paper; then troops of many uniforms marching past Napoleon.
shots.anim: Flags of many colours pass the camera.

shots.vo: The Russians retreated and burned what they left behind. At Borodino they finally stood and fought. Tens of thousands died in one day, and the Russians pulled back again.
shots.visual: Burning fields and villages; then Borodino: smoke over a redoubt, cannon fire, a line of Russian soldiers withdrawing.
shots.anim: Smoke rolls; cannons flash; the Russian line steps back.

shots.vo: He reached Moscow in September. It was nearly empty. Then it burned.
shots.visual: Napoleon on a hill looking at the domes of Moscow; at night the city glows with fire.
shots.anim: Fire spreads across the skyline; sparks rise.

shots.vo: He waited five weeks for a peace offer. None came. In October he turned back, and winter caught him.
shots.visual: Napoleon pacing in a Kremlin room by a fire; snowflakes start at the window.
shots.anim: He looks at the window; the first flakes fall.

shots.vo: Cold, hunger, Cossack raids, the river crossing at the Berezina. By December the Grande Armée was gone.
shots.visual: The snow road: soldiers wrapped in blankets; horses down; a crowd crossing a broken wooden bridge over an icy river.
shots.anim: Snow howls; the bridge sways; the hat lies in the snow.

shots.vo: Now Europe knew he could be beaten. Russia, Prussia, Austria, Sweden and Britain joined together. At Leipzig in 1813, about half a million soldiers fought for three days, and Napoleon lost.
shots.visual: The Europe map: allied arrows close in from all sides; then a vast battlefield of smoke around a city.
shots.anim: Arrows squeeze the blue; smoke fills the frame.

shots.vo: In April 1814, with enemies in Paris and his own marshals refusing to fight, he gave up his throne at Fontainebleau.
shots.visual: A palace room: Napoleon alone at a desk, a pen in hand; his marshals standing by the door, looking away.
shots.anim: The pen hovers, then signs; a marshal closes the door.

shots.vo: They sent him to rule the tiny island of Elba. He lasted less than a year.
shots.visual: Elba: a small harbour; Napoleon walking on a terrace, staring at the sea toward France.
shots.anim: Waves; he shades his eyes toward the horizon.

shots.vo: In March 1815 he landed in France with about a thousand men. The king's soldiers blocked the road. Napoleon walked toward them alone and opened his coat. 'If any of you wants to kill his emperor, here I am.'
shots.visual: A country road near Grenoble: a line of soldiers with muskets raised; Napoleon walking toward them alone in a grey coat.
shots.anim: Muskets tremble; he opens his coat.

shots.vo: Nobody fired. They cheered and joined him. Three weeks later he was back in Paris, and the king had fled.
shots.visual: Soldiers throwing their caps in the air and running to him; then Paris crowds.
shots.anim: Caps fly; crowds surge.

shots.vo: On the eighteenth of June 1815, near the village of Waterloo, he attacked Wellington's British-led army. Hour after hour, Wellington's line held. Then the Prussians arrived on his flank.
shots.visual: A muddy ridge; British squares; French cavalry charging; in the distance, Prussian columns coming out of a wood.
shots.anim: Cavalry thunders; smoke; the Prussian flags appear.

shots.vo: He sent in the Imperial Guard. At close range, the British line stood up and fired. The Guard fell back, and the whole French army broke.
shots.visual: Bearskin-hatted Guard marching uphill; redcoats rise from the wheat and fire; the Guard turns; the bicorne hat on the mud.
shots.anim: A wall of smoke; the Guard's line breaks.

shots.vo: This time, the British sent him to Saint Helena, a speck of rock in the South Atlantic, nearly two thousand kilometres from Africa.
shots.visual: A British warship approaching a steep black island under grey clouds.
shots.anim: The ship rolls; clouds cling to the cliffs.

shots.vo: He lived in a damp house called Longwood, dictating his memoirs, arguing with his guards, and gardening.
shots.visual: Foggy Longwood House; Napoleon, older and heavier, in a garden with a hoe; a British sentry watching.
shots.anim: Fog drifts; he leans on the hoe.

shots.vo: He died on the fifth of May 1821, aged fifty-one, most likely of stomach cancer. His last words were reported as: France, the army, Josephine.
shots.visual: A dim bedroom; a few servants by the bed; a candle; the window with the grey sea.
shots.anim: The candle flame bends and goes out.

shots.vo: What he left still matters. His legal code of 1804 shaped the laws of dozens of countries. He spread the idea of equal citizens across Europe.
shots.visual: A printed book: CODE CIVIL; pages fly off it onto a world map, landing on country after country.
shots.anim: Pages flutter onto the map.

shots.vo: The price was huge too. His wars killed somewhere between three and a half and six million people.
shots.visual: A field of white crosses fading into the distance under a grey sky.
shots.anim: Slow push across the crosses.

shots.vo: Napoleon had everything. He could have stopped. But there was always one more crown, one more war. In the end, he was left with an island and the sea.
shots.visual: The bicorne hat on a hook at Longwood; through the window, the empty grey sea.
shots.anim: Slow push to the window; fade out.

hooks: In 1812 Napoleon led more than 600,000 men into Russia. Only a small fraction came back.
He crowned himself emperor with his own hands. Eleven years later he was on a rock in the Atlantic.

fixes: Source: 'His brother sat on the thrones of Spain, Holland and Westphalia' by 1805. Wrong date: Joseph became King of Naples in 1806 and of Spain in 1808, Louis King of Holland in 1806, Jérôme King of Westphalia in 1807. Script puts it after Austerlitz and names Naples, Holland, Westphalia, with Spain in 1808.
Source: the Holy Roman Empire 'collapsed within weeks' of Austerlitz. It was dissolved on 6 Aug 1806, about eight months later. Script: 'within a year'.
Source: 'that same year (1808) he divorced Josephine'. The divorce was in Dec 1809 / Jan 1810; married Marie Louise April 1810; son born March 1811.
Source: in Russia 'the final battle never came'. Wrong: the Battle of Borodino, 7 Sept 1812, one of the bloodiest single days of the era (~70,000 casualties). Added.

Grande Armée crossed the Neman on 24 June 1812; total force including reinforcements was over 600,000. Survivors are disputed (often given as under 100,000, some say far fewer). Script says 'only a small fraction'.
Source: Waterloo was 'two days' after crossing into Belgium on 15 June. It was three days (Ligny and Quatre Bras on 16 June, Waterloo on 18 June).
Source: first abdication 'April 4th'. Napoleon signed a conditional abdication on 4 April and an unconditional one on 6 April 1814. Script: 'April 1814'.
Source: Saint Helena is 'the most remote inhabited island in the world'. Wrong (Tristan da Cunha is more remote). Script: nearly 2,000 km from Africa.
Source: his last word was 'Josephine'. Reported last words were 'France, armée, tête d'armée, Joséphine'. Script gives France, the army, Josephine.
Source: poisoning theory presented as open. Stomach cancer is the accepted cause; arsenic theories are widely rejected. Script: 'most likely of stomach cancer'.
Source: Napoleonic Wars killed '3 to 6 million soldiers'. Common estimates are about 3.5 to 6 million deaths in total, soldiers and civilians. Fixed.
Laffrey, 7 March 1815: the 5th Line Infantry; his words are usually given as 'If there is a soldier among you who wishes to kill his emperor, here I am.'
Egypt expedition took about 167 scholars (the savants); fleet destroyed at the Battle of the Nile, 1 Aug 1798. He left Egypt in Aug 1799.
Napoleon became an artillery lieutenant in 1785, aged 16. Promoted brigadier general after Toulon (Dec 1793).
Height: about 1.69 m (5 ft 7), average for his time; the 'short' myth comes from French vs English inches and British cartoons (reel only).
cuts: Cut the language-learner pace, the repeated refrain (used once in the cold open idea only), and the 'Era Speak' channel outro. Merged the Josephine divorce into the Russia act as the lead-in.
